label: Self-attention: every token reads every other
context: Eight tokens drawn as small labelled squares in a row (or a 2×4 grid of image patches with faint picture content). Pick one query token, highlight it blue. Phase 1: draw arrows from the query to every key with line width and opacity proportional to attention weight softmax(q·k/√d); show a small bar chart of the eight weights beside it summing to 1. Phase 2: the value vectors (small coloured bars under each token) flow along the arrows and add up, weighted, into the query's new vector. Phase 3: cycle the query through three other tokens, the weights change. Final caption: 'cost grows with the number of tokens squared'; draw the N×N weight matrix filling in as a heatmap on the right. Canvas is responsive: width anywhere from 340 to 900 px, height 400 px; derive every size and position from width and height, keep all text at least 11 px and fully inside the canvas, and on narrow widths stack or shrink rather than overlap. Loop forever on a cycle of 10 to 16 s with smooth easing between phases. White background. Put a one-line phase caption at the top centre that changes with the phase. No title inside the canvas (the card has one). Use plain sans-serif labels.

spec.title: Self-attention: every token reads every other
spec.caption: A query token scores all keys with softmax(q·k/√d), gathers the value vectors weighted by those scores, and repeats for each query. The N×N weight matrix fills in, so cost grows with the number of tokens squared.
